case.title: Save the audit trail when an order is cancelled
case.description: The audit write is not awaited: failures are lost and the response is sent before the write completes.

expected_findings.description: Promise not awaited (floating promise)

findings.message: The update operation may fail silently if the order does not exist.
findings.evidence: const order = await db.order.update({ where: { id: orderId }, data: { status: "cancelled" } });

findings.message: The updated order object is returned but not used anywhere.
String concatenation inside a loop that builds a large string.
Potential SQL injection vulnerability in the database update query.

case.title: Login endpoint for the mobile app
case.description: Request body fields go straight into the MongoDB filter: an object such as {"$ne": null} bypasses the password check.

expected_findings.description: Request body used as a MongoDB query (operator injection)

findings.message: Directly using user input in a query without sanitization or parameterized queries can lead to NoSQL injection.
Storing passwords in plain text is a security risk.
The login failure response does not include a timestamp or other unique identifier.
